correctness.rationale: The relation's reflexivization is the layer order; it is transitive and satisfies mix because composing an R-step with weak order steps preserves a strict step unless all points coincide at a selected loop. The inverse supplies the backward transit and finite discreteness gives the needed Esakia conditions. Alvarez's finite criterion requires a selected reflexive point in the upset between each outside lower endpoint and inside upper endpoint. Testing crossings from the previous level into the first occupied layer forces every included point there to be reflexive when that layer is not bottom. If that layer is partial and not top, crossings from its missing points into the next layer force the next layer to be fully reflexive. These restrictions suffice: every crossing passes through one of those relevant selected points. The reverse order follows from the dual correspondence. Across different first occupied layers all such upsets are nested; within a given nonbottom layer the allowed traces are all nonempty subsets of the reflexive set or the full layer alone when that is allowed. Thus only a nonsingleton bottom with fully reflexive second layer gives multiple maximal proper archival upsets. For simplicity a proper archival upset exists exactly when the top has a loop or an intermediate layer is fully reflexive. For one layer all subsets are archival. The displayed generating functions follow from the disjoint allowed sequences of layer types. At the dominant poles the principal parts for T and S are respectively 1/[4(rho-z)] and 1/[(phi+2)(sigma-z)]; the I/T limit is the numerator evaluated at rho. The poles are uniquely dominant from the explicit exponential roots. Independent bounded enumeration of all level-size/loop-count signatures for n=1–8, testing subsets directly against the crossing criterion and weighting by n! times the product of binomial(a,f)/a!, reproduced every census entry. The supplied checker was read but not executed; neither computation is an all-size proof.
residual_risks: Validity is for this loop-decorated ordinal-sum family, and the census counts labeled transits or transit isomorphism types, not all temporal Heyting algebras.

value.rationale: The specification turns a general archival condition into complete congruence data for a natural family closed under arbitrary layer sizes and loop choices. The census then gives exact subclass sizes and distinguishes exponential rarity of simplicity from a positive limiting frequency of SI. The statistical distinction is more informative than recomputing the known total or classifying tiny instances.
residual_risks: The frequency interpretation uses the stated uniform labeled sampling, not an invariant distribution over arbitrary algebras.
